issues.description: The problem specification declares calculateRemainingOrderNumber() as returning an int (UML and textual description), but the example usage in the problem shows printed lines (suggesting a void method that prints order numbers). The provided solution implements calculateRemainingOrderNumber() as a void method that prints order numbers instead of returning an int. This inconsistency between the problem statement and the solution (and the internal contradiction in the problem statement between the method signature and the example) will confuse students about the expected behavior and return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expectation consistent. Either: (A) Change the problem statement/UML to specify calculateRemainingOrderNumber() is void and documents that it prints "Order number: ..." lines (then keep or adjust the solution to correctly print the intended sequence), or (B) Keep calculateRemainingOrderNumber() returning int (as currently in UML/text) and update the solution to return the integer number of remaining orders (and remove/relocate any printing). Also correct the example in the problem statement to match the chosen behavior.
